properties.description: Copper coordinated with 4 nitrogen atoms in nitrogen-doped graphene

nodes.characterization_summary: HADDF-STEM images exhibit atomic dispersion of single Pt atoms (bright dots marked with yellow circles) on ultrathin CTF nanosheets support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the HADDF-STEM images shown in Figure 3a clearly exhibit the atomic dispersion of heavy single Pt atoms (bright dots) on the ultrathin covalent triazine frameworks (CTF) nanosheets support which are marked with yellow circles.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows isolated bright dots (≈1.2 Å) as Mo single atoms in O,S co-doped graphene; pseudo-color surface plot reveals preferential Mo SA locations along defective edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Tang et al. employed HAADF-STEM analysis and verified the numerous isolated bright dots (≈1.2Å inset of Figure 3c) as Mo single atoms in the O, S co-doped graphene (Figure 3c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows ordered lattice fringes (0.371 nm spacing corresponding to WO3 (100) plane); isolated brighter dots (heavier than W) are Pt atoms substituting W positions or vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ordered lattice fringes by bright dots can be clearly observed with the estimated lattice spacing of 0.371 nm, corresponding to (100) plane of the cubic WO3 support (Figure 3e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic resolution STEM shows hexagonal MoS2 lattice; enlarged image reveals embedded Ni atoms (red cross) confirmed by EELS Ni peaks at ≈855 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the enlarged image from inner region 1 (Figure 3h) clearly showed several embedded foreign atoms (marked with red cross) in the MoS2 atomic column, which were revealed as Ni atoms by the corresponding EELS spectrum with Ni peaks at ≈855 eV (Figure 3i).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms uniform Ni distribution and existence of Ni SAs (bright dots, average size ≈0.24 nm) due to abundant defects as anchoring sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM image (Figure 4b) presents the existence of Ni SAs with high atomic loadings (bright dots with average site of ≈0.24 nm) in the A-Ni@DG, in contrast to defect-free graphene.

nodes.characterization_summary: Low-temperature STM image shows bright spot corresponding to iron center with well-defined FeN4 moiety embedded in graphene lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4g clearly presents a representative STM image with high atomic resolution in which the bright spot corresponds to iron center and adjacent atoms (N and C atoms) can be distinguished.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu K-edge XANES absorption edge of Cu-N4-NG between CuPc (Cu(II), 8984.4 eV) and Cu foil (Cu(0), 8978.9 eV) indicates intermediate Cuδ+ (δ=0-2) oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Cu K-edge XANES spectra in Figure 5a show that the absorption edge of Cu-N4-NG occurs between the CuPc reference (Cu(II), 8984.4 eV) and Cu foil reference (metallic Cu(0) 8978.9 eV)

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Cu-N peak at 1.48 Å (no Cu-Cu peak at 2.21 Å); EXAFS fitting validates Cu-N4 coordination environment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both CuPc and Cu-N4-NG possess the dominant peak at 1.48 Å corresponding to Cu-N while no obvious Cu-Cu peaks (2.21 Å) can be found in Cu-N4-NG ... the fitting result derived from the Cu-N4 model structure matches well with experimental EXAFS data

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS at Co K-edge shows exclusive Co-S bonds at 1.79 Å for atomic Co dispersed on distorted 1T MoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the FT-EXAFS spectra at the Co K-edge demonstrate the exclusive presence of Co-S bonds at 1.79 Å for atomic Co dispersed on distorted 1T MoS2 (SA Co-D 1T MoS2, Figure 5d).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of Ni species across defective graphene.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STEM-EDS elemental mapping of A-Ni@DG (Figure 4a) confirms the uniform distribution of Ni species across the defective graphene.

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS spectrum shows Ni peaks at ≈855 eV confirming embedded Ni atoms in MoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: which were revealed as Ni atoms by the corresponding EELS spectrum with Ni peaks at ≈855 eV (Figure 3i).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge XANES shows gradual decrease of white-line peak intensity across PtSA-NiO, PtSA-NiO/Ni, PtSA-Ni supports indicating varied Pt charge depletion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Pt L3-edge XANES spectra of isolated Pt atoms on various nanosheets supports obviously show the gradual decrease of white-line peak intensity upon changing the support from NiO, NiO/Ni to Ni

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows no Pt-Pt peak at 2.7 Å confirming atomic dispersion; first-shell fitting gives CN 1.3 Pt-O/5.8 Pt-Ni for PtSA-NiO/Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the corresponding FT-EXAFS spectra ... unraveled the coordination configurations of Pt SAs ... absence of the typical Pt-Pt peak at about 2.7 Å ... the first-shell EXAFS fitting ... demonstrated the coordination number (CN) of 1.3 for Pt-O and 5.8 for Pt-Ni in PtSA-NiO/Ni
